# I. Data Loading and PCA Setup

This section loads the dataset and defines the variables for principal component analysis. The code specifies PCA variables including yield metrics, climate variables (temperature, humidity, rainfall indices), and soil temperature measurements. It reads the CSV file, extracts the relevant columns, and performs initial data cleaning by removing observations with missing values. The PCA is executed with both centering and scaling to standardize variables with different units and magnitudes, ensuring fair contribution to the principal components.

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Read the dataset

# Define variables for PCA
pca_vars <- c('tc_per_ha_actual','brix_percent', 'growing_season_rainfall_mm', 'temp_mini_mean', 'temp_maxi_mean', 
              'temp_moy_mean', 'ampl_mean', 'h_mini_mean', 'h_maxi_mean', 'h_moy_mean', 
              'h_6h_mean', 'h_12h_mean', 'h_16h_mean', 'h_24h_mean', 'soil_temp_6h_mean', 
              'soil_temp_16h_mean', 'radiation_ERA_total', 'evaporation_total', 'CWD', 
              'CDD', 'SDII', 'R10', 'R20', 'Rx1', 'Rx5', 'R95p', 'R99p', 'HD', 
              'TNn', 'TNx', 'TXn', 'TXx')

# Select and prepare data (remove NAs)
pca_data <- data %>%
  select(all_of(pca_vars)) %>%
  na.omit()

# Perform PCA (with scaling)
pca_result <- prcomp(pca_data, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Extract variance explained
variance_explained <- (pca_result$sdev^2) / sum(pca_result$sdev^2) * 100
cumulative_variance <- cumsum(variance_explained)

# Create data frame for plotting
pca_df <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(variance_explained),
  Variance = variance_explained,
  Cumulative = cumulative_variance
)


p <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC)) +
  # Individual variance (bars)
  geom_col(aes(y = Variance), fill = "#2E86AB", alpha = 0.7, width = 0.7) +
  
  # Cumulative variance (line)
  geom_line(aes(y = Cumulative), color = "#A23B72", size = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = Cumulative), color = "#A23B72", size = 2.5) +
  
  # Reference lines for 80%, 90%, 95%
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = "#E63946", size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed", color = "#F77F00", size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 95, linetype = "dashed", color = "#06A77D", size = 0.8) +
  
  # Add text labels for reference lines
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df$PC) * 0.95, y = 80, label = "80%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 5, color = "#E63946", fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df$PC) * 0.95, y = 90, label = "90%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 5, color = "#F77F00", fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df$PC) * 0.95, y = 95, label = "95%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 5, color = "#06A77D", fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Scales and labels
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, max(pca_df$PC), by = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20)) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Principal Component",
    y = "Variance Explained (%)",
    title = "PCA Scree Plot"
  ) +
  
  # Nature journal style theme
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    # Text elements
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    
    # Lines
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.8),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    
    # Panel
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    
    # Remove grid
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Display the plot
print(p)

# Save the plot (high resolution for publication)
ggsave("pca_scree_plot.png", plot = p, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("pca_scree_plot.pdf", plot = p, width = 7, height = 5, device = "pdf")

# Print summary statistics
cat("\n=== PCA Summary ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Total variables: %d\n", length(pca_vars)))
cat(sprintf("Number of observations: %d\n", nrow(pca_data)))
cat("\nVariance explained by first 10 PCs:\n")
print(round(variance_explained[1:10], 2))
cat("\nCumulative variance explained:\n")
print(round(cumulative_variance[1:10], 2))

# Find number of PCs needed for 80%, 90%, 95%
n_pcs_80 <- which(cumulative_variance >= 80)[1]
n_pcs_90 <- which(cumulative_variance >= 90)[1]
n_pcs_95 <- which(cumulative_variance >= 95)[1]

cat(sprintf("\nNumber of PCs for 80%% variance: %d\n", n_pcs_80))
cat(sprintf("Number of PCs for 90%% variance: %d\n", n_pcs_90))
cat(sprintf("Number of PCs for 95%% variance: %d\n", n_pcs_95))
getwd()
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# FUNCTION TO CREATE BIPLOT FOR ANY DIM COMBINATION (Enhanced)
# ============================================================================
create_biplot <- function(pca_result, dim1, dim2, variance_explained, 
                          color_by = "cos2", use_short_names = TRUE) {
  # Extract loadings
  loadings <- pca_result$rotation[, c(dim1, dim2)]
  
  # Calculate cos2
  cos2 <- loadings^2
  cos2_total <- cos2[, 1] + cos2[, 2]
  
  # Calculate contributions
  contrib <- loadings^2 / matrix(pca_result$sdev[c(dim1, dim2)]^2, 
                                  nrow = nrow(loadings), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE) * 100
  contrib_total <- contrib[, 1] + contrib[, 2]
  
  # Get variable names (short or long)
  var_names <- rownames(loadings)
  if (use_short_names) {
    var_names <- sapply(var_names, function(x) {
      if (x %in% names(variable_name_map)) {
        variable_name_map[x]
      } else {
        x
      }
    })
  }
  
  # Create data frame
  arrow_df <- data.frame(
    variable = var_names,
    original_name = rownames(loadings),
    Dim1 = loadings[, 1],
    Dim2 = loadings[, 2],
    cos2 = cos2_total,
    contrib = contrib_total,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Scaling factor
  scale_factor <- 0.8 * max(sqrt(rowSums(loadings^2)))
  
  # Choose color variable and palette (colorblind-friendly)
  if (color_by == "cos2") {
    color_var <- arrow_df$cos2
    color_name <- "cos²"
    # Viridis scale (excellent for colorblind)
    color_scale <- scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724"),
      name = color_name,
      guide = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        title.hjust = 0.5,
        barwidth = 0.8,
        barheight = 8
      )
    )
  } else {
    color_var <- arrow_df$contrib
    color_name <- "Contrib (%)"
    # Blue-Yellow scale (colorblind-friendly)
    color_scale <- scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724"),
      name = color_name,
      guide = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        title.hjust = 0.5,
        barwidth = 0.8,
        barheight = 8
      )
    )
  }
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(arrow_df, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = Dim1 * scale_factor, 
                            yend = Dim2 * scale_factor)) +
    geom_segment(aes(color = color_var), 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"), 
                 linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(x = Dim1 * scale_factor * 1.15, 
                  y = Dim2 * scale_factor * 1.15, 
                  label = variable, 
                  color = color_var), 
              size = 2.5, fontface = "bold", check_overlap = FALSE) +
    color_scale +
    labs(x = sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", dim1, variance_explained[dim1]),
         y = sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", dim2, variance_explained[dim2]),
         title = sprintf("PC%d vs PC%d", dim1, dim2)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 9, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "cm"),
      legend.key.width = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    ) +
    coord_fixed()
  
  return(p)
}

cat("\n=== Creating enhanced PCA visualizations ===\n")

# Create all pairwise combinations with cos2

  create_biplot(pca_result, 1, 2, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 1, 3, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 1, 4, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 2, 3, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 2, 4, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 2, 5, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 3, 4, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 3, 5, variance_explained, "cos2"),
  create_biplot(pca_result, 4, 5, variance_explained, "cos2")
)

# Arrange in 3x3 grid
grid_cos2 <- arrangeGrob(
  grobs = dim_pairs_cos2, 
  ncol = 3, 
  nrow = 3,
  top = textGrob("PCA Biplots - Quality of Representation (cos²)", 
                gp = gpar(fontsize = 18, fontface = "bold"))
)

       width = 18, height = 18, dpi = 600, bg = "white")

       width = 18, height = 18, device = cairo_pdf)

# Arrange in 3x3 grid

cat(sprintf("Number of PCs for 95%% variance: %d (%.2f%%)\n", 
            n_pcs_95, cumulative_variance[n_pcs_95]))

# Calculate overall cos2 and contribution for PC1-PC2
loadings_12 <- pca_result$rotation[, 1:2]
cos2_12 <- rowSums(loadings_12^2)
contrib_12 <- rowSums(loadings_12^2) / sum(pca_result$sdev[1:2]^2) * 100

# Apply short names
names(cos2_12) <- sapply(names(cos2_12), function(x) {
  if (x %in% names(variable_name_map)) variable_name_map[x] else x
})
names(contrib_12) <- names(cos2_12)

cat("\n=== Top 15 variables by cos² (PC1-PC2) ===\n")
top_cos2 <- data.frame(variable = names(cos2_12), cos2 = cos2_12)
top_cos2 <- top_cos2[order(-top_cos2$cos2), ][1:15, ]
rownames(top_cos2) <- NULL
print(top_cos2)

cat("\n=== Top 15 variables by contribution (PC1-PC2) ===\n")
top_contrib <- data.frame(variable = names(contrib_12), contrib = contrib_12)
top_contrib <- top_contrib[order(-top_contrib$contrib), ][1:15, ]
rownames(top_contrib) <- NULL
print(top_contrib)

# ============================================================================
# CREATE SUMMARY REPORT
# ============================================================================
cat("\n=== Creating summary report ===\n")

# Loadings for PC1-PC5
loadings_summary <- as.data.frame(pca_result$rotation[, 1:5])
loadings_summary$Variable <- rownames(loadings_summary)
loadings_summary$Short_Name <- sapply(loadings_summary$Variable, function(x) {
  if (x %in% names(variable_name_map)) variable_name_map[x] else x
})

# Reorder columns
loadings_summary <- loadings_summary[, c("Variable", "Short_Name", "PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "PC4", "PC5")]
loadings_summary <- loadings_summary[order(-abs(loadings_summary$PC1)), ]

write.csv(loadings_summary, "pca_loadings_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)


# Select and prepare data (remove NAs)
pca_data <- data %>%
  select(all_of(pca_vars)) %>%
  na.omit()

# Perform PCA (with scaling)
pca_result <- prcomp(pca_data, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Calculate variance explained for each dimension
variance_explained <- (pca_result$sdev^2) / sum(pca_result$sdev^2) * 100

# ============================================================================
# CREATE CONTRIBUTION TABLE
# ============================================================================

# Get loadings (rotation matrix)
loadings <- pca_result$rotation

# Calculate contributions for each dimension
# Contribution = (loading^2 / eigenvalue) * 100
# where eigenvalue = sdev^2
eigenvalues <- pca_result$sdev^2

# Initialize contribution matrix
n_vars <- nrow(loadings)
n_dims <- ncol(loadings)
contributions <- matrix(0, nrow = n_vars, ncol = n_dims)

# Calculate contributions
for (i in 1:n_dims) {
  contributions[, i] <- (loadings[, i]^2 / eigenvalues[i]) * 100
}

# Create data frame with variable names (rounded to 3 decimals)
contrib_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(loadings),
  round(contributions, 3)
)

# Rename columns to Dim1, Dim2, etc.
colnames(contrib_df) <- c("Variable", paste0("Dim", 1:n_dims))

# ============================================================================
# DETERMINE NUMBER OF DIMENSIONS FOR 80% VARIANCE
# ============================================================================

# Calculate cumulative variance
cumulative_variance <- cumsum(variance_explained)

# Find number of dimensions needed for 80% variance
n_dims_80 <- which(cumulative_variance >= 80)[1]

cat("\n=== Variance Threshold Analysis ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of dimensions for 80%% variance: %d\n", n_dims_80))
cat(sprintf("Actual cumulative variance with %d dimensions: %.3f%%\n", 
            n_dims_80, cumulative_variance[n_dims_80]))

# ============================================================================
# ALSO CREATE COS2 TABLE (Quality of representation)
# ============================================================================

# Calculate cos2 for each dimension (rounded to 3 decimals)
cos2_matrix <- round(loadings^2, 3)

# Create cos2 data frame
cos2_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(loadings),
  cos2_matrix
)

colnames(cos2_df) <- c("Variable", paste0("Dim", 1:n_dims, "_cos2"))

# ============================================================================
# CREATE COMBINED TABLE WITH BOTH METRICS
# ============================================================================

# Use only dimensions up to 80% variance
n_dims_export <- n_dims_80

# Create combined table
combined_df <- data.frame(Variable = rownames(loadings))

for (i in 1:n_dims_export) {
  # Add contribution column (3 decimals)
  combined_df[[paste0("Dim", i, "_contrib")]] <- round(contributions[, i], 3)
  # Add cos2 column (3 decimals)
  combined_df[[paste0("Dim", i, "_cos2")]] <- round(loadings[, i]^2, 3)
  # Add loading column (3 decimals)
  combined_df[[paste0("Dim", i, "_loading")]] <- round(loadings[, i], 3)
}

# ============================================================================
# SAVE TO CSV FILES
# ============================================================================

# Save contribution table
write.csv(contrib_df[, 1:(n_dims_export+1)], 
          "pca_contributions.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)

# Save cos2 table
write.csv(cos2_df[, 1:(n_dims_export+1)], 
          "pca_cos2.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)

# Save combined table
write.csv(combined_df, 
          "pca_combined_metrics.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)

# ============================================================================
# CREATE SUMMARY TABLE WITH TOP CONTRIBUTORS PER DIMENSION
# ============================================================================

# For each dimension, get top 5 contributors
top_contributors <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:n_dims_export) {
  dim_contrib <- data.frame(
    Dimension = paste0("Dim", i),
    Variance_Explained = round(variance_explained[i], 3),
    Variable = rownames(loadings),
    Contribution = round(contributions[, i], 3),
    Cos2 = round(loadings[, i]^2, 3),
    Loading = round(loadings[, i], 3)
  )
  
  # Sort by contribution and take top 5
  dim_contrib <- dim_contrib[order(-dim_contrib$Contribution), ][1:5, ]
  dim_contrib$Rank <- 1:5
  
  top_contributors <- rbind(top_contributors, dim_contrib)
}

# Save top contributors
write.csv(top_contributors, 
          "pca_top_contributors.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)


variance_table <- data.frame(
  Dimension = paste0("Dim", 1:n_dims_export),
  Variance_Percent = round(variance_explained[1:n_dims_export], 3),
  Cumulative_Percent = round(cumsum(variance_explained)[1:n_dims_export], 3)
)
print(variance_table)

cat("\n=== Preview: Top 5 Contributors to Dim 1 ===\n")
dim1_top <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(loadings),
  Contribution = round(contributions[, 1], 3),
  Cos2 = round(loadings[, 1]^2, 3)
)
dim1_top <- dim1_top[order(-dim1_top$Contribution), ][1:5, ]
print(dim1_top)

cat("\n=== Preview: Top 5 Contributors to Dim 2 ===\n")
dim2_top <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(loadings),
  Contribution = round(contributions[, 2], 3),
  Cos2 = round(loadings[, 2]^2, 3)
)
dim2_top <- dim2_top[order(-dim2_top$Contribution), ][1:5, ]
print(dim2_top)
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(gridExtra)
library(grid)

# ============================================================================
# VARIABLE NAME MAPPING (Long to Short) - SOIL ONLY
# ============================================================================
variable_name_map <- c(
  # Soil chemical properties
  "pH_complete" = "pH",
  "Exchangeable_Calcium_meq_100g_complete" = "Exch_Ca",
  "Exchangeable_Magnesium_meq_100g_complete" = "Exch_Mg",
  "Exchangeable_Potassium_meq_100g_complete" = "Exch_K",
  "Exchangeable_Sodium_meq_100g_complete" = "Exch_Na",
  "Available_P2O5_mg_kg_complete" = "Avail_P",
  "Total_Nitrogen_per_mille_complete" = "Total_N",
  "Organic_Carbon_per_mille_complete" = "Org_C",
  "Electrical_Conductivity_mmho_cm_complete" = "EC",
  
  # Soil physical properties
  "Clay_percent_complete" = "Clay",
  "Fine_Silt_percent_complete" = "Fine_Silt",
  "Coarse_Silt_percent_complete" = "Coarse_Silt",
  "Fine_Sand_percent_complete" = "Fine_Sand",
  "Coarse_Sand_percent_complete" = "Coarse_Sand",
  "Compaction_Index_complete" = "Compact_Idx",
  
  # Soil ratios
  "Mg_K_Ratio_complete" = "Mg:K",
  "Mg_Ca_Ratio_complete" = "Mg:Ca"
)

# Define SOIL variables for PCA
pca_vars_soil <- c(
  "pH_complete",
  "Exchangeable_Calcium_meq_100g_complete",
  "Exchangeable_Magnesium_meq_100g_complete",
  "Exchangeable_Potassium_meq_100g_complete",
  "Exchangeable_Sodium_meq_100g_complete",
  "Available_P2O5_mg_kg_complete",
  "Total_Nitrogen_per_mille_complete",
  "Organic_Carbon_per_mille_complete",
  "Electrical_Conductivity_mmho_cm_complete",
  "Clay_percent_complete",
  "Fine_Silt_percent_complete",
  "Coarse_Silt_percent_complete",
  "Fine_Sand_percent_complete",
  "Coarse_Sand_percent_complete",
  "Compaction_Index_complete",
  "Mg_K_Ratio_complete",
  "Mg_Ca_Ratio_complete"
)

# Select and prepare data (remove NAs)
pca_data_soil <- data %>%
  select(all_of(pca_vars_soil)) %>%
  na.omit()

# Perform PCA (with scaling)
pca_result_soil <- prcomp(pca_data_soil, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Extract variance explained
variance_explained_soil <- (pca_result_soil$sdev^2) / sum(pca_result_soil$sdev^2) * 100
cumulative_variance_soil <- cumsum(variance_explained_soil)

# Create data frame for scree plot
pca_df_soil <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(variance_explained_soil),
  Variance = variance_explained_soil,
  Cumulative = cumulative_variance_soil
)

# ============================================================================
# COLORBLIND-FRIENDLY PALETTES
# ============================================================================
# Viridis palette (colorblind-friendly) for cos2
viridis_colors <- c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724")

# Tol bright scheme (colorblind-friendly) for highlights
tol_colors <- list(
  blue = "#4477AA",
  red = "#EE6677",
  green = "#228833",
  yellow = "#CCBB44",
  cyan = "#66CCEE",
  purple = "#AA3377",
  grey = "#BBBBBB"
)

# ============================================================================
# SCREE PLOT (Enhanced) - SOIL
# ============================================================================
p_scree_soil <- ggplot(pca_df_soil, aes(x = PC)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = Variance), fill = tol_colors$blue, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cumulative), color = tol_colors$purple, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = Cumulative), color = tol_colors$purple, size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = tol_colors$red, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed", color = tol_colors$yellow, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 95, linetype = "dashed", color = tol_colors$green, linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df_soil$PC) * 0.85, y = 80, label = "80%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 4, color = tol_colors$red, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df_soil$PC) * 0.85, y = 90, label = "90%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 4, color = tol_colors$yellow, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df_soil$PC) * 0.85, y = 95, label = "95%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 4, color = tol_colors$green, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, max(pca_df_soil$PC), by = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 25)) +
  labs(x = "Principal Component", y = "Variance Explained (%)", 
       title = "Scree Plot - PCA Variance Explained (Soil Variables)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.7),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )

# ============================================================================
# FUNCTION TO CREATE BIPLOT FOR ANY DIM COMBINATION (Enhanced) - SOIL
# ============================================================================
create_biplot_soil <- function(pca_result, dim1, dim2, variance_explained, 
                               color_by = "cos2", use_short_names = TRUE) {
  # Extract loadings
  loadings <- pca_result$rotation[, c(dim1, dim2)]
  
  # Calculate cos2
  cos2 <- loadings^2
  cos2_total <- cos2[, 1] + cos2[, 2]
  
  # Calculate contributions
  contrib <- loadings^2 / matrix(pca_result$sdev[c(dim1, dim2)]^2, 
                                  nrow = nrow(loadings), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE) * 100
  contrib_total <- contrib[, 1] + contrib[, 2]
  
  # Get variable names (short or long)
  var_names <- rownames(loadings)
  if (use_short_names) {
    var_names <- sapply(var_names, function(x) {
      if (x %in% names(variable_name_map)) {
        variable_name_map[x]
      } else {
        x
      }
    })
  }
  
  # Create data frame
  arrow_df <- data.frame(
    variable = var_names,
    original_name = rownames(loadings),
    Dim1 = loadings[, 1],
    Dim2 = loadings[, 2],
    cos2 = cos2_total,
    contrib = contrib_total,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Scaling factor
  scale_factor <- 0.8 * max(sqrt(rowSums(loadings^2)))
  
  # Choose color variable and palette (colorblind-friendly)
  if (color_by == "cos2") {
    color_var <- arrow_df$cos2
    color_name <- "cos²"
    # Viridis scale (excellent for colorblind)
    color_scale <- scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724"),
      name = color_name,
      guide = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        title.hjust = 0.5,
        barwidth = 0.8,
        barheight = 8
      )
    )
  } else {
    color_var <- arrow_df$contrib
    color_name <- "Contrib (%)"
    # Blue-Yellow scale (colorblind-friendly)
    color_scale <- scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724"),
      name = color_name,
      guide = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        title.hjust = 0.5,
        barwidth = 0.8,
        barheight = 8
      )
    )
  }
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(arrow_df, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = Dim1 * scale_factor, 
                            yend = Dim2 * scale_factor)) +
    geom_segment(aes(color = color_var), 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed"), 
                 linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(x = Dim1 * scale_factor * 1.15, 
                  y = Dim2 * scale_factor * 1.15, 
                  label = variable, 
                  color = color_var), 
              size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", check_overlap = FALSE) +
    color_scale +
    labs(x = sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", dim1, variance_explained[dim1]),
         y = sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", dim2, variance_explained[dim2]),
         title = sprintf("PC%d vs PC%d", dim1, dim2)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 9, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "cm"),
      legend.key.width = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    ) +
    coord_fixed()
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# CREATE 3x3 GRID OF BIPLOTS (COLORED BY COS2) - SOIL
# ============================================================================

# Determine which dimensions to plot (first 5 or until 95% variance)
n_dims_soil <- min(5, which(cumulative_variance_soil >= 95)[1])
if (is.na(n_dims_soil)) n_dims_soil <- min(5, length(variance_explained_soil))

cat("Creating 3x3 grid colored by cos² (Soil)...\n")

# Create all pairwise combinations with cos2
dim_pairs_cos2_soil <- list(
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 2, variance_explained_soil, "cos2"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 3, variance_explained_soil, "cos2"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 4, variance_explained_soil, "cos2"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 2, 3, variance_explained_soil, "cos2"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 2, 4, variance_explained_soil, "cos2"),

  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 3, 4, variance_explained_soil, "cos2"),

# Arrange in 3x3 grid

  nrow = 3,
  top = textGrob("PCA Biplots - Soil Variables - Quality of Representation (cos²)", 
                gp = gpar(fontsize = 18, fontface = "bold"))

# Save and display

       width = 18, height = 18, dpi = 600, bg = "white")

dim_pairs_contrib_soil <- list(
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 2, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 3, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 4, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 2, 3, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 2, 4, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 2, 5, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 3, 4, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 3, 5, variance_explained_soil, "contrib"),
  create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 4, 5, variance_explained_soil, "contrib")
)

# Arrange in 3x3 grid
grid_contrib_soil <- arrangeGrob(
  grobs = dim_pairs_contrib_soil, 
  ncol = 3, 
  nrow = 3,
  top = textGrob("PCA Biplots - Soil Variables - Variable Contributions", 
                gp = gpar(fontsize = 18, fontface = "bold"))
)

# Save and display
ggsave("pca_soil_grid_contrib_enhanced.png", grid_contrib_soil, 
       width = 18, height = 18, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("pca_soil_grid_contrib_enhanced.pdf", grid_contrib_soil, 
       width = 18, height = 18, device = cairo_pdf)
grid.draw(grid_contrib_soil)

# ============================================================================
# SAVE INDIVIDUAL PLOTS (LARGER SIZE) - SOIL
# ============================================================================
cat("Saving individual plots (Soil)...\n")

# Scree plot
ggsave("pca_soil_scree_plot_enhanced.png", plot = p_scree_soil, 
       width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave("pca_soil_scree_plot_enhanced.pdf", plot = p_scree_soil, 
       width = 8, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)

# Save individual PC1 vs PC2 plots (larger for detail)
p_cos2_main_soil <- create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 2, variance_explained_soil, "cos2") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),

  )

p_contrib_main_soil <- create_biplot_soil(pca_result_soil, 1, 2, variance_explained_soil, "contrib") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),

ggsave("pca_soil_biplot_cos2_enhanced.png", plot = p_cos2_main_soil,
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================================
# VARIABLE NAME MAPPING (Long to Short) - CLIMATE ONLY
# ============================================================================
variable_name_map_climate <- c(
  # Temperature
  "temp_mini_mean" = "T_min",
  "temp_maxi_mean" = "T_max",
  "temp_moy_mean" = "T_mean",
  "ampl_mean" = "T_ampl",
  "TNn" = "TNn",
  "TNx" = "TNx",
  "TXn" = "TXn",
  "TXx" = "TXx",
  
  # Humidity
  "h_mini_mean" = "RH_min",
  "h_maxi_mean" = "RH_max",
  "h_moy_mean" = "RH_mean",
  "h_6h_mean" = "RH_6h",
  "h_12h_mean" = "RH_12h",
  "h_16h_mean" = "RH_16h",
  "h_24h_mean" = "RH_24h",
  
  # Soil temperature
  "soil_temp_6h_mean" = "Soil_T_6h",
  "soil_temp_16h_mean" = "Soil_T_16h",
  
  # Radiation and evaporation
  "radiation_ERA_total" = "Radiation",
  "evaporation_total" = "Evaporation",
  
  # Precipitation indices
  "growing_season_rainfall_mm" = "GS_Rain",
  "CWD" = "CWD",
  "CDD" = "CDD",
  "SDII" = "SDII",
  "R10" = "R10",
  "R20" = "R20",
  "Rx1" = "Rx1",
  "Rx5" = "Rx5",
  "R95p" = "R95p",
  "R99p" = "R99p",
  "HD" = "HD"
)

# Define CLIMATE variables for PCA
pca_vars_climate <- c(
  "growing_season_rainfall_mm",
  "temp_mini_mean",
  "temp_maxi_mean",
  "temp_moy_mean",
  "ampl_mean",
  "h_mini_mean",
  "h_maxi_mean",
  "h_moy_mean",
  "h_6h_mean",
  "h_12h_mean",
  "h_16h_mean",
  "h_24h_mean",
  "soil_temp_6h_mean",
  "soil_temp_16h_mean",
  "radiation_ERA_total",
  "evaporation_total",
  "CWD",
  "CDD",
  "SDII",
  "R10",
  "R20",
  "Rx1",
  "Rx5",
  "R95p",
  "R99p",
  "HD",
  "TNn",
  "TNx",
  "TXn",
  "TXx"
)

# Select and prepare data (remove NAs)
pca_data_climate <- data %>%
  select(all_of(pca_vars_climate)) %>%
  na.omit()

# Perform PCA (with scaling)
pca_result_climate <- prcomp(pca_data_climate, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Extract variance explained
variance_explained_climate <- (pca_result_climate$sdev^2) / sum(pca_result_climate$sdev^2) * 100
cumulative_variance_climate <- cumsum(variance_explained_climate)

# Create data frame for scree plot
pca_df_climate <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:length(variance_explained_climate),
  Variance = variance_explained_climate,
  Cumulative = cumulative_variance_climate
)

# ============================================================================
# COLORBLIND-FRIENDLY PALETTES
# ============================================================================
# Viridis palette (colorblind-friendly) for cos2
viridis_colors <- c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724")

# Tol bright scheme (colorblind-friendly) for highlights
tol_colors <- list(
  blue = "#4477AA",
  red = "#EE6677",
  green = "#228833",
  yellow = "#CCBB44",
  cyan = "#66CCEE",
  purple = "#AA3377",
  grey = "#BBBBBB"
)

# ============================================================================
# SCREE PLOT (Enhanced) - CLIMATE
# ============================================================================
p_scree_climate <- ggplot(pca_df_climate, aes(x = PC)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = Variance), fill = tol_colors$blue, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Cumulative), color = tol_colors$purple, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = Cumulative), color = tol_colors$purple, size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = tol_colors$red, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed", color = tol_colors$yellow, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 95, linetype = "dashed", color = tol_colors$green, linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df_climate$PC) * 0.95, y = 80, label = "80%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 4, color = tol_colors$red, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df_climate$PC) * 0.95, y = 90, label = "90%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 4, color = tol_colors$yellow, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = max(pca_df_climate$PC) * 0.95, y = 95, label = "95%", 
           vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1, size = 4, color = tol_colors$green, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, max(pca_df_climate$PC), by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 25)) +
  labs(x = "Principal Component", y = "Variance Explained (%)", 
       title = "Scree Plot - PCA Variance Explained (Climate Variables)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.7),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )

# ============================================================================
# FUNCTION TO CREATE BIPLOT FOR ANY DIM COMBINATION (Enhanced) - CLIMATE
# ============================================================================
create_biplot_climate <- function(pca_result, dim1, dim2, variance_explained, 
                                  color_by = "cos2", use_short_names = TRUE) {
  # Extract loadings
  loadings <- pca_result$rotation[, c(dim1, dim2)]
  
  # Calculate cos2
  cos2 <- loadings^2
  cos2_total <- cos2[, 1] + cos2[, 2]
  
  # Calculate contributions
  contrib <- loadings^2 / matrix(pca_result$sdev[c(dim1, dim2)]^2, 
                                  nrow = nrow(loadings), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE) * 100
  contrib_total <- contrib[, 1] + contrib[, 2]
  
  # Get variable names (short or long)
  var_names <- rownames(loadings)
  if (use_short_names) {
    var_names <- sapply(var_names, function(x) {
      if (x %in% names(variable_name_map_climate)) {
        variable_name_map_climate[x]
      } else {
        x
      }
    })
  }
  
  # Create data frame
  arrow_df <- data.frame(
    variable = var_names,
    original_name = rownames(loadings),
    Dim1 = loadings[, 1],
    Dim2 = loadings[, 2],
    cos2 = cos2_total,
    contrib = contrib_total,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Scaling factor
  scale_factor <- 0.8 * max(sqrt(rowSums(loadings^2)))
  
  # Choose color variable and palette (colorblind-friendly)
  if (color_by == "cos2") {
    color_var <- arrow_df$cos2
    color_name <- "cos²"
    # Viridis scale (excellent for colorblind)
    color_scale <- scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724"),
      name = color_name,
      guide = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        title.hjust = 0.5,
        barwidth = 0.8,
        barheight = 8
      )
    )
  } else {
    color_var <- arrow_df$contrib
    color_name <- "Contrib (%)"
    # Blue-Yellow scale (colorblind-friendly)
    color_scale <- scale_color_gradientn(
      colors = c("#440154", "#31688E", "#35B779", "#FDE724"),
      name = color_name,
      guide = guide_colorbar(
        title.position = "top",
        title.hjust = 0.5,
        barwidth = 0.8,
        barheight = 8
      )
    )
  }
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(arrow_df, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = Dim1 * scale_factor, 
                            yend = Dim2 * scale_factor)) +
    geom_segment(aes(color = color_var), 
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"), 
                 linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(x = Dim1 * scale_factor * 1.15, 
                  y = Dim2 * scale_factor * 1.15, 
                  label = variable, 
                  color = color_var), 
              size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", check_overlap = FALSE) +
    color_scale +
    labs(x = sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", dim1, variance_explained[dim1]),
         y = sprintf("PC%d (%.1f%%)", dim2, variance_explained[dim2]),
         title = sprintf("PC%d vs PC%d", dim1, dim2)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 9, color = "black"),
      axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
      legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "cm"),
      legend.key.width = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    ) +
    coord_fixed()
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================

  if (x %in% names(variable_name_map_climate)) variable_name_map_climate[x] else x
})

# Reorder columns
col_order <- c("Variable", "Short_Name", paste0("PC", 1:n_pcs_show))
loadings_summary_climate <- loadings_summary_climate[, col_order]
loadings_summary_climate <- loadings_summary_climate[order(-abs(loadings_summary_climate$PC1)), ]

write.csv(loadings_summary_climate, "pca_climate_loadings_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create correlation circle data
cor_circle_climate <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(cos2_12_climate),
  PC1 = loadings_12_climate[, 1],
  PC2 = loadings_12_climate[, 2],
  cos2 = cos2_12_climate,
  contrib = contrib_12_climate
)
write.csv(cor_circle_climate, "pca_climate_correlation_circle.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# II. INLA Model Validation Plots

This final section creates journal-style scatter plots comparing observed versus predicted values for all imputed soil variables. The code generates both individual high-resolution plots and combined grids organized by variable groups (granulometry, exchangeable nutrients, other properties, and ILR coordinates). Each plot includes detailed performance metrics for training and validation datasets with R², RMSE, and correlation coefficients displayed using color-coded annotations. The visualizations follow publication standards with equal aspect ratios, 1:1 reference lines, regression confidence bands, and bilingual labels (French and English) to support international journal submission. All plots are saved at 600 DPI in both PNG and PDF formats with consistent styling across individual and combined presentations.

```{r}
# ============================================================================
#  COMBINED GRID PLOTS
# All variables in a single multi-panel figure
# ============================================================================

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)

library(patchwork)  # For combining plots

cat("========================================\n")

cat("========================================\n")

# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
cat("📂 LOADING DATA:\n")

base_path <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/clean_soil_dataset/"
gpkg_all_vars <- paste0(base_path, "parcels_ALL_VARIABLES_enhanced_predictions.gpkg")

if (!file.exists(gpkg_all_vars)) {

}

parcelles_all <- st_read(gpkg_all_vars, quiet = TRUE)
cat("✅ Data loaded:", nrow(parcelles_all), "observations\n")

# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
output_dir <- "C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy/journal_grid_plots"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

cat("Output directory:", output_dir, "\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: DEFINE VARIABLES AND CUSTOM LABELS
# ============================================================================

ALL_VARS <- c(
  "Clay_percent",
  "Fine_Silt_percent",
  "Coarse_Silt_percent",
  "Fine_Sand_percent",
  "Coarse_Sand_percent",
  "pH",
  "Exchangeable_Calcium_meq_100g",
  "Exchangeable_Magnesium_meq_100g", 
  "Exchangeable_Potassium_meq_100g",
  "Organic_Carbon_per_mille",
  "Total_Nitrogen_per_mille",
  "Mg_Ca_Ratio",
  "Mg_K_Ratio"
)

CUSTOM_LABELS <- c(
  "Clay (%)",
  "Fine Silt (%)",
  "Coarse Silt (%)",
  "Fine Sand (%)",
  "Coarse Sand (%)",
  "pH",
  "Exch. Ca (meq/100g)",
  "Exch. Mg (meq/100g)",
  "Exch. K (meq/100g)",
  "Organic C (‰)",
  "Total N (‰)",
  "Mg/Ca Ratio",
  "Mg/K Ratio"
)

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: JOURNAL-STYLE PLOTTING FUNCTION (Returns ggplot object)
# ============================================================================

create_journal_plot_object <- function(var_name, var_label, data_sf, verbose = TRUE) {
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("📊", var_name, "\n")
  }
  
  # Column names
  pred_col <- paste0(var_name, "_predicted")
  pred_type_col <- paste0(var_name, "_prediction_type")
  
  # Check columns exist
  if (!pred_col %in% colnames(data_sf) || !pred_type_col %in% colnames(data_sf)) {
    if (verbose) {
      cat("  ⚠️ Skipping - columns not found\n")
    }
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract and prepare data
  plot_data <- data_sf %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var_name]]), !is.na(.data[[pred_col]])) %>%
    mutate(
      Observed = .data[[var_name]],
      Predicted = .data[[pred_col]],
      Dataset = factor(
        case_when(
          .data[[pred_type_col]] == "Training" | .data[[pred_type_col]] == "train" ~ "Training",
          .data[[pred_type_col]] == "Validation" | .data[[pred_type_col]] == "validation" ~ "Validation",
          TRUE ~ "Other"
        ),
        levels = c("Training", "Validation")
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Dataset), is.finite(Observed), is.finite(Predicted))
  
  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ No valid data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Calculate metrics by dataset
  train_data <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Training")
  val_data <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Validation")
  
  if (nrow(train_data) < 5 || nrow(val_data) < 5) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ Insufficient data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  train_r2 <- cor(train_data$Observed, train_data$Predicted)^2
  val_r2 <- cor(val_data$Observed, val_data$Predicted)^2
  train_corr <- cor(train_data$Observed, train_data$Predicted)
  val_corr <- cor(val_data$Observed, val_data$Predicted)
  
  train_rmse <- sqrt(mean((train_data$Observed - train_data$Predicted)^2))
  val_rmse <- sqrt(mean((val_data$Observed - val_data$Predicted)^2))
  
  # Determine axis limits
  all_vals <- c(plot_data$Observed, plot_data$Predicted)
  val_range <- range(all_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  val_span <- diff(val_range)
  axis_limits <- c(val_range[1] - 0.05 * val_span, val_range[2] + 0.05 * val_span)
  
  # Create plot (same style as original)
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted, color = Dataset, fill = Dataset)) +
    # 1:1 reference line
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Smooth regression lines
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
    
    # Data points
    geom_point(aes(shape = Dataset), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75, stroke = 0.3) +
    
    # Color scheme
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#0072B2", "Validation" = "#D55E00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#56B4E9", "Validation" = "#E69F00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Training" = 16, "Validation" = 17),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    
    # Equal aspect ratio
    coord_equal(xlim = axis_limits, ylim = axis_limits) +
    
    # Labels
    labs(
      x = paste0("Observed"),
      y = paste0("Predicted"),
      title = var_label
    ) +
    
    # Metrics annotation (smaller for grid)
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = axis_limits[1] + 0.05 * val_span,
      y = axis_limits[2] - c(0.08, 0.15, 0.22) * val_span,
      label = c(
        sprintf("Train: R²=%.2f", train_r2),
        sprintf("Valid: R²=%.2f", val_r2),
        sprintf("RMSE: %.2f/%.2f", train_rmse, val_rmse)
      ),
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 2.8,
      color = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "black"),
      fontface = c("bold", "bold", "plain")
    ) +
    
    # Theme
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.3),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey30", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("  ✓ Train: R²=", round(train_r2, 3), ", Valid: R²=", round(val_r2, 3), "\n")
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: ILR TRANSFORMATION FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

create_ilr_basis <- function(D) {
  V <- matrix(0, nrow = D - 1, ncol = D)
  for (i in 1:(D - 1)) {
    V[i, 1:i] <- 1/i
    V[i, i + 1] <- -1
    V[i, ] <- V[i, ] * sqrt(i / (i + 1))
  }
  return(V)
}

ilr_transform <- function(composition_matrix) {
  D <- ncol(composition_matrix)
  V <- create_ilr_basis(D)
  log_comp <- log(composition_matrix)
  ilr_coords <- log_comp %*% t(V)
  return(ilr_coords)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: ILR PLOT FUNCTION
# ============================================================================

create_journal_plot_object_ilr <- function(ilr_index, data_sf, verbose = TRUE) {
  
  ilr_var <- paste0("ILR_", ilr_index)
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("📊", ilr_var, "\n")
  }
  
  # Check for complete granulometry data
  GRANULO_FRACTIONS <- c(
    "Clay_percent",
    "Fine_Silt_percent",
    "Coarse_Silt_percent",
    "Fine_Sand_percent",
    "Coarse_Sand_percent"
  )
  
  comp_data <- data_sf %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(!is.na(Clay_percent), 
           !is.na(Fine_Silt_percent),
           !is.na(Coarse_Silt_percent),
           !is.na(Fine_Sand_percent),
           !is.na(Coarse_Sand_percent)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(ILR_1_predicted))
  
  if (nrow(comp_data) == 0) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ No compositional data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Determine dataset split
  if ("Clay_percent_prediction_type" %in% colnames(comp_data)) {
    comp_data <- comp_data %>%
      mutate(Dataset = factor(
        case_when(
          Clay_percent_prediction_type == "train" ~ "Training",
          Clay_percent_prediction_type == "validation" ~ "Validation",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        levels = c("Training", "Validation")
      ))
  } else {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ No prediction type\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  comp_data <- comp_data %>% filter(!is.na(Dataset))
  
  # Split data
  train_data <- comp_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Training")
  val_data <- comp_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Validation")
  
  if (nrow(train_data) < 5 || nrow(val_data) < 5) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ Insufficient data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Compute observed ILR
  train_comp <- train_data %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(GRANULO_FRACTIONS)) %>%
    as.matrix()
  train_comp[train_comp <= 0] <- 0.01
  train_comp <- train_comp / rowSums(train_comp) * 100
  train_ilr <- ilr_transform(train_comp / 100)
  
  val_comp <- val_data %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(GRANULO_FRACTIONS)) %>%
    as.matrix()
  val_comp[val_comp <= 0] <- 0.01
  val_comp <- val_comp / rowSums(val_comp) * 100
  val_ilr <- ilr_transform(val_comp / 100)
  
  # Prepare plot data
  pred_col <- paste0("ILR_", ilr_index, "_predicted")
  
  plot_data <- bind_rows(
    train_data %>% mutate(
      Observed = train_ilr[, ilr_index],
      Predicted = .data[[pred_col]]
    ),
    val_data %>% mutate(
      Observed = val_ilr[, ilr_index],
      Predicted = .data[[pred_col]]
    )
  ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(Observed), is.finite(Predicted))
  
  # Calculate metrics
  train_subset <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Training")
  val_subset <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Validation")
  
  train_r2 <- cor(train_subset$Observed, train_subset$Predicted)^2
  val_r2 <- cor(val_subset$Observed, val_subset$Predicted)^2
  
  train_rmse <- sqrt(mean((train_subset$Observed - train_subset$Predicted)^2))
  val_rmse <- sqrt(mean((val_subset$Observed - val_subset$Predicted)^2))
  
  # Axis limits
  all_vals <- c(plot_data$Observed, plot_data$Predicted)
  val_range <- range(all_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  val_span <- diff(val_range)
  axis_limits <- c(val_range[1] - 0.05 * val_span, val_range[2] + 0.05 * val_span)
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted, color = Dataset, fill = Dataset)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = Dataset), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75, stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#0072B2", "Validation" = "#D55E00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#56B4E9", "Validation" = "#E69F00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Training" = 16, "Validation" = 17),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    coord_equal(xlim = axis_limits, ylim = axis_limits) +
    labs(
      x = "Observed",
      y = "Predicted",
      title = paste0("ILR", ilr_index)
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = axis_limits[1] + 0.05 * val_span,
      y = axis_limits[2] - c(0.08, 0.15, 0.22) * val_span,
      label = c(
        sprintf("Train: R²=%.2f", train_r2),
        sprintf("Valid: R²=%.2f", val_r2),
        sprintf("RMSE: %.2f/%.2f", train_rmse, val_rmse)
      ),
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 2.8,
      color = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "black"),
      fontface = c("bold", "bold", "plain")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.3),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey30", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("  ✓ Train: R²=", round(train_r2, 3), ", Valid: R²=", round(val_r2, 3), "\n")
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 7: CREATE ALL PLOT OBJECTS
# ============================================================================
cat("\n🔄 CREATING PLOT OBJECTS:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 42), "\n", sep="")

plot_list <- list()

# Create plots for all variables
cat("\n[ALL VARIABLES]\n")
for (i in seq_along(ALL_VARS)) {
  var_name <- ALL_VARS[i]
  var_label <- CUSTOM_LABELS[i]
  cat(sprintf("[%2d/%2d] ", i, length(ALL_VARS)))
  
  p <- create_journal_plot_object(var_name, var_label, parcelles_all, verbose = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    plot_list[[var_name]] <- p
  }
}

# Create ILR plots
cat("\n[ILR COORDINATES]\n")
for (i in 1:4) {
  cat(sprintf("[%2d/%2d] ", i, 4))
  
  p <- create_journal_plot_object_ilr(i, parcelles_all, verbose = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    plot_list[[paste0("ILR_", i)]] <- p
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 8: DETERMINE OPTIMAL GRID LAYOUT
# ============================================================================
n_plots <- length(plot_list)
cat("\n📐 DETERMINING GRID LAYOUT:\n")
cat("  Total plots:", n_plots, "\n")

# Find optimal grid dimensions (as square as possible)
n_cols <- ceiling(sqrt(n_plots))
n_rows <- ceiling(n_plots / n_cols)

cat("  Grid dimensions:", n_rows, "×", n_cols, "\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 9: COMBINE PLOTS INTO GRID
# ============================================================================
cat("\n🎨 COMBINING PLOTS INTO GRID:\n")

# Use patchwork to combine plots
combined_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = n_cols, nrow = n_rows)

# Add a common title and caption
combined_plot <- combined_plot +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Model Performance: Observed vs Predicted Values",
    subtitle = "Training (blue) and Validation (orange) datasets",
    caption = "Dashed red line = 1:1 reference. Shaded bands = 95% confidence intervals.",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey30"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey50")
    )
  )

# ============================================================================
# STEP 10: SAVE COMBINED GRID
# ============================================================================
cat("\n💾 SAVING COMBINED GRID:\n")

# Calculate figure dimensions (each subplot ~60mm, plus margins)
subplot_width_mm <- 60
subplot_height_mm <- 60
margin_mm <- 20

total_width_mm <- n_cols * subplot_width_mm + margin_mm
total_height_mm <- n_rows * subplot_height_mm + margin_mm + 30  # +30 for title

cat("  Figure dimensions:", total_width_mm, "×", total_height_mm, "mm\n")

# Save PNG
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "combined_grid_all_variables.png"),
  combined_plot,
  width = total_width_mm,
  height = total_height_mm,
  units = "mm",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

# Save PDF
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "combined_grid_all_variables.pdf"),
  combined_plot,
  width = total_width_mm,
  height = total_height_mm,
  units = "mm",
  device = cairo_pdf,
  bg = "white"
)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: JOURNAL-STYLE PLOTTING FUNCTION FOR ORIGINAL VARS
# ============================================================================

create_journal_plot_object <- function(var_name, var_label, data_sf, verbose = TRUE) {
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("📊", var_name, "\n")
  }
  
  # Column names
  pred_col <- paste0(var_name, "_predicted")
  pred_type_col <- paste0(var_name, "_prediction_type")
  
  # Check columns exist
  if (!pred_col %in% colnames(data_sf) || !pred_type_col %in% colnames(data_sf)) {
    if (verbose) {
      cat("  ⚠️ Skipping - columns not found\n")
    }
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract and prepare data
  plot_data <- data_sf %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[var_name]]), !is.na(.data[[pred_col]])) %>%
    mutate(
      Observed = .data[[var_name]],
      Predicted = .data[[pred_col]],
      Dataset = factor(
        case_when(
          .data[[pred_type_col]] == "Training" | .data[[pred_type_col]] == "train" ~ "Training",
          .data[[pred_type_col]] == "Validation" | .data[[pred_type_col]] == "validation" ~ "Validation",
          TRUE ~ "Other"
        ),
        levels = c("Training", "Validation")
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Dataset), is.finite(Observed), is.finite(Predicted))
  
  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ No valid data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Calculate metrics by dataset
  train_data <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Training")
  val_data <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Validation")
  
  if (nrow(train_data) < 5 || nrow(val_data) < 5) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ Insufficient data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  train_r2 <- cor(train_data$Observed, train_data$Predicted)^2
  val_r2 <- cor(val_data$Observed, val_data$Predicted)^2
  
  train_rmse <- sqrt(mean((train_data$Observed - train_data$Predicted)^2))
  val_rmse <- sqrt(mean((val_data$Observed - val_data$Predicted)^2))
  
  # Determine axis limits
  all_vals <- c(plot_data$Observed, plot_data$Predicted)
  val_range <- range(all_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  val_span <- diff(val_range)
  axis_limits <- c(val_range[1] - 0.05 * val_span, val_range[2] + 0.05 * val_span)
  
  # Create plot (same style as original)
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted, color = Dataset, fill = Dataset)) +
    # 1:1 reference line
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2) +
    
    # Smooth regression lines
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
    
    # Data points
    geom_point(aes(shape = Dataset), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75, stroke = 0.3) +
    
    # Color scheme
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#0072B2", "Validation" = "#D55E00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#56B4E9", "Validation" = "#E69F00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Training" = 16, "Validation" = 17),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    
    # Equal aspect ratio
    coord_equal(xlim = axis_limits, ylim = axis_limits) +
    
    # Labels
    labs(
      x = "Observed",
      y = "Predicted",
      title = var_label
    ) +
    
    # Metrics annotation (smaller for grid)
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = axis_limits[1] + 0.05 * val_span,
      y = axis_limits[2] - c(0.08, 0.15, 0.22) * val_span,
      label = c(
        sprintf("Train: R²=%.2f", train_r2),
        sprintf("Valid: R²=%.2f", val_r2),
        sprintf("RMSE: %.2f/%.2f", train_rmse, val_rmse)
      ),
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 2.8,
      color = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "black"),
      fontface = c("bold", "bold", "plain")
    ) +
    
    # Theme
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.3),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey30", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("  ✓ Train: R²=", round(train_r2, 3), ", Valid: R²=", round(val_r2, 3), "\n")
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: JOURNAL-STYLE PLOTTING FUNCTION FOR ENHANCED VARS
# ============================================================================

create_journal_plot_object_enhanced <- function(var_name, var_label, data_sf, verbose = TRUE) {
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("📊", var_name, "(enhanced)\n")
  }
  
  # Column names
  pred_col <- paste0(var_name, "_predicted")
  pred_type_col <- paste0(var_name, "_prediction_type")
  
  # Find original variable column
  possible_original_names <- c(
    var_name,
    gsub("_", "", var_name),
    paste0(var_name, "_original")
  )
  
  original_col <- NULL
  for (name in possible_original_names) {
    if (name %in% colnames(data_sf)) {
      original_col <- name
      break
    }
  }
  
  if (is.null(original_col)) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ Original variable column not found\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Check required columns exist
  required_cols <- c(original_col, pred_col, pred_type_col)
  missing_cols <- required_cols[!required_cols %in% colnames(data_sf)]
  
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ Missing columns:", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract and prepare data
  plot_data <- data_sf %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[original_col]]), !is.na(.data[[pred_col]])) %>%
    mutate(
      Observed = .data[[original_col]],
      Predicted = .data[[pred_col]],
      Dataset = factor(
        case_when(
          .data[[pred_type_col]] == "Training" | .data[[pred_type_col]] == "train" ~ "Training",
          .data[[pred_type_col]] == "Validation" | .data[[pred_type_col]] == "validation" ~ "Validation",
          TRUE ~ "Other"
        ),
        levels = c("Training", "Validation")
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Dataset), is.finite(Observed), is.finite(Predicted))
  
  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ No valid data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Calculate metrics by dataset
  train_data <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Training")
  val_data <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Validation")
  
  if (nrow(train_data) < 5 || nrow(val_data) < 5) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ Insufficient data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  train_r2 <- cor(train_data$Observed, train_data$Predicted)^2
  val_r2 <- cor(val_data$Observed, val_data$Predicted)^2
  
  train_rmse <- sqrt(mean((train_data$Observed - train_data$Predicted)^2))
  val_rmse <- sqrt(mean((val_data$Observed - val_data$Predicted)^2))
  
  # Determine axis limits
  all_vals <- c(plot_data$Observed, plot_data$Predicted)
  val_range <- range(all_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  val_span <- diff(val_range)
  axis_limits <- c(val_range[1] - 0.05 * val_span, val_range[2] + 0.05 * val_span)
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted, color = Dataset, fill = Dataset)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = Dataset), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75, stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#0072B2", "Validation" = "#D55E00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#56B4E9", "Validation" = "#E69F00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Training" = 16, "Validation" = 17),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    coord_equal(xlim = axis_limits, ylim = axis_limits) +
    labs(
      x = "Observed",
      y = "Predicted",
      title = var_label
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = axis_limits[1] + 0.05 * val_span,
      y = axis_limits[2] - c(0.08, 0.15, 0.22) * val_span,
      label = c(
        sprintf("Train: R²=%.2f", train_r2),
        sprintf("Valid: R²=%.2f", val_r2),
        sprintf("RMSE: %.2f/%.2f", train_rmse, val_rmse)
      ),
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 2.8,
      color = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "black"),
      fontface = c("bold", "bold", "plain")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.3),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey30", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("  ✓ Train: R²=", round(train_r2, 3), ", Valid: R²=", round(val_r2, 3), "\n")
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: ILR TRANSFORMATION FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

create_ilr_basis <- function(D) {
  V <- matrix(0, nrow = D - 1, ncol = D)
  for (i in 1:(D - 1)) {
    V[i, 1:i] <- 1/i
    V[i, i + 1] <- -1
    V[i, ] <- V[i, ] * sqrt(i / (i + 1))
  }
  return(V)
}

ilr_transform <- function(composition_matrix) {
  D <- ncol(composition_matrix)
  V <- create_ilr_basis(D)
  log_comp <- log(composition_matrix)
  ilr_coords <- log_comp %*% t(V)
  return(ilr_coords)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 7: ILR PLOT FUNCTION
# ============================================================================

create_journal_plot_object_ilr <- function(ilr_index, data_sf, verbose = TRUE) {
  
  ilr_var <- paste0("ILR_", ilr_index)
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("📊", ilr_var, "\n")
  }
  
  # Check for complete granulometry data
  GRANULO_FRACTIONS <- c(
    "Clay_percent",
    "Fine_Silt_percent",
    "Coarse_Silt_percent",
    "Fine_Sand_percent",
    "Coarse_Sand_percent"
  )
  
  comp_data <- data_sf %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(!is.na(Clay_percent), 
           !is.na(Fine_Silt_percent),
           !is.na(Coarse_Silt_percent),
           !is.na(Fine_Sand_percent),
           !is.na(Coarse_Sand_percent)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(ILR_1_predicted))
  
  if (nrow(comp_data) == 0) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ No compositional data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Determine dataset split
  if ("Clay_percent_prediction_type" %in% colnames(comp_data)) {
    comp_data <- comp_data %>%
      mutate(Dataset = factor(
        case_when(
          Clay_percent_prediction_type == "train" ~ "Training",
          Clay_percent_prediction_type == "validation" ~ "Validation",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        levels = c("Training", "Validation")
      ))
  } else {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ No prediction type\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  comp_data <- comp_data %>% filter(!is.na(Dataset))
  
  # Split data
  train_data <- comp_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Training")
  val_data <- comp_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Validation")
  
  if (nrow(train_data) < 5 || nrow(val_data) < 5) {
    if (verbose) cat("  ⚠️ Insufficient data\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Compute observed ILR
  train_comp <- train_data %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(GRANULO_FRACTIONS)) %>%
    as.matrix()
  train_comp[train_comp <= 0] <- 0.01
  train_comp <- train_comp / rowSums(train_comp) * 100
  train_ilr <- ilr_transform(train_comp / 100)
  
  val_comp <- val_data %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(GRANULO_FRACTIONS)) %>%
    as.matrix()
  val_comp[val_comp <= 0] <- 0.01
  val_comp <- val_comp / rowSums(val_comp) * 100
  val_ilr <- ilr_transform(val_comp / 100)
  
  # Prepare plot data
  pred_col <- paste0("ILR_", ilr_index, "_predicted")
  
  plot_data <- bind_rows(
    train_data %>% mutate(
      Observed = train_ilr[, ilr_index],
      Predicted = .data[[pred_col]]
    ),
    val_data %>% mutate(
      Observed = val_ilr[, ilr_index],
      Predicted = .data[[pred_col]]
    )
  ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(Observed), is.finite(Predicted))
  
  # Calculate metrics
  train_subset <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Training")
  val_subset <- plot_data %>% filter(Dataset == "Validation")
  
  train_r2 <- cor(train_subset$Observed, train_subset$Predicted)^2
  val_r2 <- cor(val_subset$Observed, val_subset$Predicted)^2
  
  train_rmse <- sqrt(mean((train_subset$Observed - train_subset$Predicted)^2))
  val_rmse <- sqrt(mean((val_subset$Observed - val_subset$Predicted)^2))
  
  # Axis limits
  all_vals <- c(plot_data$Observed, plot_data$Predicted)
  val_range <- range(all_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  val_span <- diff(val_range)
  axis_limits <- c(val_range[1] - 0.05 * val_span, val_range[2] + 0.05 * val_span)
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted, color = Dataset, fill = Dataset)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = Dataset), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.75, stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#0072B2", "Validation" = "#D55E00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Training" = "#56B4E9", "Validation" = "#E69F00"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Training" = 16, "Validation" = 17),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    coord_equal(xlim = axis_limits, ylim = axis_limits) +
    labs(
      x = "Observed",
      y = "Predicted",
      title = paste0("ILR", ilr_index)
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = axis_limits[1] + 0.05 * val_span,
      y = axis_limits[2] - c(0.08, 0.15, 0.22) * val_span,
      label = c(
        sprintf("Train: R²=%.2f", train_r2),
        sprintf("Valid: R²=%.2f", val_r2),
        sprintf("RMSE: %.2f/%.2f", train_rmse, val_rmse)
      ),
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 2.8,
      color = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "black"),
      fontface = c("bold", "bold", "plain")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", size = 0.3),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey30", fill = NA, size = 0.8),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
    )
  
  if (verbose) {
    cat("  ✓ Train: R²=", round(train_r2, 3), ", Valid: R²=", round(val_r2, 3), "\n")
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# STEP 8: CREATE ALL PLOT OBJECTS IN ORGANIZED ORDER
# ============================================================================
cat("\n🔄 CREATING PLOT OBJECTS IN ORGANIZED ORDER:\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 50), "\n", sep="")

plot_list <- list()
plot_counter <- 0

# ============================================================================
# GROUP 1: GRANULOMETRY (5 plots)
# ============================================================================
cat("\n[GROUP 1: GRANULOMETRY - 5 VARIABLES]\n")
cat("-", rep("-", 48), "\n", sep="")
for (i in seq_along(GRANULO_VARS)) {
  var_name <- GRANULO_VARS[i]
  var_label <- GRANULO_LABELS[i]
  plot_counter <- plot_counter + 1
  cat(sprintf("[%2d] ", plot_counter))
  
  p <- create_journal_plot_object(var_name, var_label, parcelles_all, verbose = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    plot_list[[var_name]] <- p
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# GROUP 2: EXCHANGEABLE NUTRIENTS (4 plots)
# ============================================================================
cat("\n[GROUP 2: EXCHANGEABLE NUTRIENTS - 4 VARIABLES]\n")
cat("-", rep("-", 48), "\n", sep="")
for (i in seq_along(EXCHANGEABLE_VARS)) {
  var_name <- EXCHANGEABLE_VARS[i]
  var_label <- EXCHANGEABLE_LABELS[i]
  source_type <- EXCHANGEABLE_SOURCES[i]
  plot_counter <- plot_counter + 1
  cat(sprintf("[%2d] ", plot_counter))
  
  if (source_type == "original") {
    p <- create_journal_plot_object(var_name, var_label, parcelles_all, verbose = TRUE)
  } else {
    p <- create_journal_plot_object_enhanced(var_name, var_label, parcelles_enhanced, verbose = TRUE)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    plot_list[[var_name]] <- p
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# GROUP 3: OTHER SOIL PROPERTIES (8 plots)
# ============================================================================
cat("\n[GROUP 3: OTHER SOIL PROPERTIES - 8 VARIABLES]\n")
cat("-", rep("-", 48), "\n", sep="")
for (i in seq_along(OTHER_VARS)) {
  var_name <- OTHER_VARS[i]
  var_label <- OTHER_LABELS[i]
  source_type <- OTHER_SOURCES[i]
  plot_counter <- plot_counter + 1
  cat(sprintf("[%2d] ", plot_counter))
  
  if (source_type == "original") {
    p <- create_journal_plot_object(var_name, var_label, parcelles_all, verbose = TRUE)
  } else {
    p <- create_journal_plot_object_enhanced(var_name, var_label, parcelles_enhanced, verbose = TRUE)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    plot_list[[var_name]] <- p
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# GROUP 4: ILR COORDINATES (4 plots) - AT THE END
# ============================================================================
cat("\n[GROUP 4: ILR COORDINATES - 4 VARIABLES]\n")
cat("-", rep("-", 48), "\n", sep="")
for (i in 1:4) {
  plot_counter <- plot_counter + 1
  cat(sprintf("[%2d] ", plot_counter))
  
  p <- create_journal_plot_object_ilr(i, parcelles_all, verbose = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(p)) {
    plot_list[[paste0("ILR_", i)]] <- p
  }
}

cat("\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 50), "\n", sep="")
cat("✅ Total plots created:", length(plot_list), "\n")
cat("=", rep("=", 50), "\n", sep="")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 9: DETERMINE OPTIMAL GRID LAYOUT
# ============================================================================
n_plots <- length(plot_list)
cat("\n📐 DETERMINING GRID LAYOUT:\n")
cat("  Total plots:", n_plots, "\n")

# Find optimal grid dimensions (as square as possible)
n_cols <- ceiling(sqrt(n_plots))
n_rows <- ceiling(n_plots / n_cols)

cat("  Grid dimensions:", n_rows, "×", n_cols, "\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 10: COMBINE PLOTS INTO GRID
# ============================================================================
cat("\n🎨 COMBINING PLOTS INTO GRID:\n")

# Use patchwork to combine plots
combined_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = n_cols, nrow = n_rows)

# Add a common title and caption
combined_plot <- combined_plot +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Model Performance: Observed vs Predicted Values",
    subtitle = "Organized by groups: Granulometry (5) | Exchangeable (4) | Other Properties (8) | ILR (4)",
    caption = "Training (blue) and Validation (orange). Dashed red line = 1:1 reference. Shaded bands = 95% CI.",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey30"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey50")
    )
  )

# ============================================================================
# STEP 11: SAVE COMBINED GRID
# ============================================================================
cat("\n💾 SAVING COMBINED GRID:\n")

# Calculate figure dimensions (each subplot ~60mm, plus margins)
subplot_width_mm <- 60
subplot_height_mm <- 60
margin_mm <- 20

total_width_mm <- n_cols * subplot_width_mm + margin_mm
total_height_mm <- n_rows * subplot_height_mm + margin_mm + 35  # +35 for title/subtitle

cat("  Figure dimensions:", total_width_mm, "×", total_height_mm, "mm\n")

# Save PNG
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "combined_grid_all_variables_ENHANCED.png"),
  combined_plot,
  width = total_width_mm,
  height = total_height_mm,
  units = "mm",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

# Save PDF
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "combined_grid_all_variables_ENHANCED.pdf"),
  combined_plot,
  width = total_width_mm,
  height = total_height_mm,
  units = "mm",
  device = cairo_pdf,
  bg = "white"
)
```
